full_judgment:
11. In the State of Assam vs Ajit Kumar Sarma AIR 1965 (SC) 1196 the Indian Supreme Court held that it is only for the governing body of an aided college to decide whether to carry out any direction contained in mere administrative instructions laying down conditions for grant-in-aid under the Assam Aided Cottage Employees Rules (1960). Where the governing body chose to carry out an instruction, a teacher could not apply to the High Court for a mandamus against the State through the Director of Public Instruction for enforcement or non-enforcement of the rules, even if indirectly they might have some effect on him because of the grant-in-aid being with-held by the State in whole or in part. 

 "A part from express provision in the governing statute, locus standi to challenge the validity of sub-ordinate legislation the validity of sub-ordinate legislation may be restricted, under the court's inherent power to control its own procedure, to a particular category of persons affected by the sub-ordinate legislation, and if none of these persons chooses to challenge it the presumption of validity prevails. Such was the case in Durayappah vs Fernando where on an appeal from Ceylon, although the Privy Council was of opinion that an order of the Minister was ultra vires owing to a latent defect in the procedure prior to its being made, they nevertheless treated it as having legal effect because the party who sought to challenge it had, in their view, no locus standi to do so." 

 24. Again, the application is not bad for non Joinder of necessary or proper parties, No one will be affected except the Government if the impugned law is held to be void and no one has any cause to grumble with regard to any supposed right under unenforceable law. 

 25. The reason for the impugned order is that the "Bangladesh Mahila Samity is indulging in political activities contrary to its aims and objects and against the public interest." Neither in the order nor in the affidavits of the respondent there is any material to show the nature or manner of alleged indulgence in politics. The only assertion is that the Samity is a non-political organization. There is no material before us to indicate what aims and objects of the association were contravened. There is no disclosure what compelling public interest necessitated the impugned order. There is no averment that it was meant to provide for proper functioning or reconstitution of an institution which is the avowed object of the impugned legislation. 

 39. The President's Order 117 of 1972 was promulgated on 20th September, 1972 to provide for an extraordinary situation obtaining then in the country. Because of non availability of members, for various reasons, of different organizations the President's Order was passed as a "temporary arrangement" to provide for proper functioning and reconstitution of various institutions. If we look at the preamble of the President's Order and its article 4 then it would be clear that this was meant to be a temporary measure. After the commencement of the Constitution when the country got its fundamental law this Order, instead of withering away, found a place on the Statute Book. In 1973 by Act XXIV the Order was further amended and a provision for appointment of an Administrator was also introduced, and powers wider than those given to the Ad-hoc Committee were conferred on the Administrator.
